body.statement: In the transported coordinates, \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)\subset\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CX}}(P)\), so \(\mathcal T_P\subseteq\mathcal T_{\mathrm{CX},P}\). Extend \(P^\star\) by taking \(Y(a,z)=Y(a)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/5+a/5+2U^\star/5)\) and \(W(a,z)=W\) for every \(a,z\), with \((Y(a),W)\perp(A,Z)\mid U^\star\). Together with bounded finite support, strict cell positivity, treatment probabilities \(1/4\) and \(3/4\), positive Bernoulli residual variances, the displayed outcome bridge, and full column rank of the binary-latent-to-three-level \(Z\) probability matrix, this verifies the negative-control exposure, negative-control outcome, latent ignorability, overlap, bridge, variance, and completeness hypotheses used for ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification Theorem \(3\). The target derivatives agree on the intersection because both targets equal \(E[h_1-h_0]\). Consequently \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}\phi_{\mathrm{CX}}\) and \[V_{\mathrm{CX}}(P)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=\|\Pi_{\mathcal T_{\mathrm{CX},P}\cap\mathcal T_P^\perp}\phi_{\mathrm{CX}}\|_2^2.\] The additional normal directions are the nonredundant components of \(\overline{\operatorname{span}}(G,R)\) modulo \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{out},P}\). Exact projection at \(P^\star\) gives \(V_{\mathrm{CX}}(P^\star)=71536/30625\) and \(V_{\mathrm{CX}}(P^\star)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^\star)=1303968/66805375>0\).

body.gap: ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification Theorem \(3\) computes the canonical gradient for the outcome-bridge-only negative-control model; it does not impose or exploit simultaneous adjoint bridge solvability, whose nonredundant normals yield the exact positive gap above.
body.consumer: The comparison tells negative-control analysts when imposing an empirically credible treatment-bridge existence restriction changes the attainable variance.
